t: A crusading state ruled by the celibate knights of the Teutonic Order, who conquered the pagan Prussians between 1230 and about 1283.
From Marienburg the Grand Masters ran a castle-based administration and profited from Hanseatic grain and an amber monopoly.
Defeat at Grunwald in 1410 and the loss of West Prussia in 1466 broke it; in 1525 it became the Lutheran Duchy of Prussia.
dyk: The Order held a monopoly on Baltic amber, selling much of the raw amber to rosary makers in Lübeck and Bruges.
ev: Golden Bull of Rimini grants Prussian conquests to Grand Master Hermann von Salza
The Order absorbs the Livonian Brothers of the Sword
The Great Prussian Uprising begins, lasting until 1274
The Grand Master moves his seat from Venice to Marienburg
A Polish-Lithuanian army crushes the knights at the Battle of Grunwald
The Second Peace of Thorn cedes Royal Prussia to Poland
Albert of Brandenburg-Ansbach secularises the state as the Duchy of Prussia

f.founder: Hermann von Salza (Grand Master); Hermann Balk (first Landmeister in Prussia)
